Definition: Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Ahaz was king of Judah for sixteen years, and the record is blunt: he did not that which was right in the sight of the Lord, shutting the temple doors and trusting Assyria instead of God.
TheologicalSignificance: Ahaz is a warning, not a model. I hold his story up plainly: a king who would not ask God for a sign ended up asking a foreign king for help, and the help cost him everything.
